newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW-Analysts' view on Ericsson '96 report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Analysts' view on Ericsson '96 report.

text.p: The following are some analysts' views on Swedish telecoms group Ericsson's 1996 earnings that showed a 33 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 10.15 billion crowns and sales of 124.27 billion crowns.
"The strong order bookings are convincing. Particularly public telecommunications show a strong order intake, while radio communications' order intake also was strong.
"The increased dividend (of 2.50 crowns a share from 1.75 crowns) is a positive signal and the result was higher than expected."
"The pre-tax earnings per share were bang in line with our estimates while sales were a bit higher, which might imply margin erosion.
"The company has, however, suffered further costs related to currency exchange rates in the fourth quarter than we expected.
"The report was reasonably encouraging and our initial reaction is positive. But we need to see the break down of operating profits and other figures before we have a final view."
STOCKHOLM ANALYST WHO REQUESTED TO REMAIN ANONYMOUS
"The report gives very mixed signals as it is distorted by a consolidation of a Brazilian company, which boosted sales and order figures in the fourth quarter.
"But if you exclude the Brazilian company, which I think you should, underlying sales were also very strong in the fourth quarter and pushed profits higher.
"The financial net was, however, strangely high in the fourth quarter and we will have to look closer at that.
"The development within radio was positive and public telecoms returned to a largely acceptable level.
"I have long thought that the share is trading at high levels and although the report gives mixed signals it will not change my view of this price level."
